source: APPP / MAFF-JICA — Rice Seed Production Manual (សៀវភៅមគ្គទេសក៍ផលិតកម្មពូជស្រូវ), 2014, Agricultural Productivity Promotion Project in West Tonle Sap, p.36
text: After threshing, harvested seed paddy should be dried promptly to prevent quality loss: (1) Spread the threshed paddy out on a tarp/mat right after threshing so it does not sit heaped and self-heat; it should be spread in a thin layer, commonly worked into ridged rows to expose more surface to sun and allow turning. (2) Dry the paddy in the sun, turning/raking it periodically to form even ridges ('sun and shade' furrow pattern) for uniform drying. (3) Check moisture regularly with a grain-moisture meter; the paddy should be dried down to below 13% moisture before it is bagged. A drying-pile depth of roughly 10 cm is used as a practical guide for how thick to spread the grain for effective sun drying. The manual specifically warns against drying seed paddy on a paved/asphalt road surface, since it can pick up tar/asphalt odor or residue and contaminate the seed.
